content.title: About
content.content: The egg burrito with sausage is a hearty breakfast or snack consisting of a soft wheat tortilla filled with scrambled eggs, pieces of boiled or smoked sausage, cheese, and sometimes vegetables. The dish is popular in Mexican‑American cuisine, quick to prepare, and easy to take on the go.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat tortillas were used instead of traditional corn.
Eggs add a high‑quality protein boost, making the burrito more filling.
Sausage contributes a distinctive smoky flavor and raises the calorie count, providing a good source of quick energy for busy mornings.
In the United States the breakfast version is often called a “breakfast burrito”.
Variations may include avocado, salsa, beans or potatoes, but the basic recipe remains simple.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and sausage together provide about 20‑25 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle repair and prolonged satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, while sausage adds niacin and riboflavin, which help energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Sausage, especially beef varieties, is a good source of heme iron, important for normal blood formation.

items.title: Provides energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from the wheat tortilla give a quick glucose boost, while fats from cheese and sausage sustain energy release.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausage often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and sausage add saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs, which can cause skin reactions or more severe symptoms.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: An egg‑sausage burrito is relatively calorie‑dense (about 400‑500 kcal), so portion control is advised for weight‑management plans.

items.title: Preservatives in sausage
items.content: Certain sausages contain nitrites and other additives that may be undesirable with frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burrito is handheld and can be warmed in a microwave or on a skillet. It is often served with salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. Adding fresh veggies—tomatoes, onion, bell pepper—boosts flavor and nutrient content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared burritos keep in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days in an airtight container. When frozen, they last up to 1 month; reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
